title: IRTriage Unified Timeline Record
description: One row of the deterministic triage timeline. Emitted as JSONL (full fidelity, one object per line) by client/internal/timeline, and as a flattened CSV for analyst tooling. THIS IS THE CONTRACT BETWEEN THE CLIENT AND THE WEB APP - neither side may change it without updating the other side and its tests.

x-determinism.rationale: A total order. Velociraptor's artifact execution order is explicitly non-deterministic and glob() ordering is unspecified, so output order must never depend on them. row_hash is the final tiebreaker, which makes the order total even for otherwise-identical rows.
x-determinism.timestampFormat: RFC3339 UTC with EXACTLY 7 fractional digits and a literal 'Z' (e.g. 2026-09-20T10:05:00.0000000Z). 7 digits matches Windows FILETIME 100ns resolution and keeps lexicographic order identical to chronological order.
x-determinism.excludedFromTimeline: Every nondeterministic value (run id, collection start/end, durations, tool versions, operator name) lives in manifest.json - NEVER in a timeline row.
x-determinism.rowHash: Lowercase hex SHA-256 over the canonical form: the UTF-8 join of [timestamp_utc, timestamp_desc, source, artifact, message, target, host, user] with 0x1F (unit separator) between fields. Also the dedupe key for SuperTimeline merging.

schema_version.description: Schema version of this row. Consumers must reject unknown major versions.

row_hash.description: SHA-256 canonical row hash. Stable tiebreaker and cross-host dedupe key.

timestamp_utc.description: The event time in UTC. Sentinel 0001-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z means 'unknown' and sorts first.

timestamp_desc.description: What this timestamp MEANS. A single source row with 4 MACB times becomes 4 timeline rows, one per meaning - this is what makes the timeline a true super-timeline rather than a record dump.

timestamp_source_field.description: The originating column name in the raw data (e.g. 'Mtime', 'System.TimeCreated.SystemTime'). Provenance for review.

source.description: Coarse evidence category. Fixed vocabulary - the web app's dashboard facets on this.

artifact.description: Producing collector: a Velociraptor artifact name (e.g. Windows.NTFS.MFT), a custom artifact (Custom.IRTriage.*), or a native collector (native:EventLog, native:RawVolume).

collector_kind.description: Which engine produced the row. Lets the analyst separate acquisition from detection.

host_id.description: Stable host identifier (machine GUID) - disambiguates same-named hosts when merging.

user.description: User associated with the event, as DOMAIN\user where known.

message.description: Deterministic human-readable summary, rendered from a FIXED per-source template. Never LLM-generated, never locale-dependent.

target.description: Primary object of the event: a file path, registry key, URL, service name, or account name.

file.description: Filesystem detail when the event concerns a file.

ads_name.description: Alternate data stream name, if any.

detections.description: Detection rules that matched THIS row. Populated by the rule-join stage. An empty array is normal and expected - the client deliberately over-collects; triage is refined downstream by the web app.

severity.description: Normalized across engines. Sigma level maps 1:1. YARA reads meta.severity, defaulting to medium. Nuclei info->informational. Hayabusa level maps 1:1.

rule_source.description: Rule pack the rule came from, e.g. sigma:core++, yara:reversinglabs, nuclei:file/keys.

mitre_techniques.description: Uppercased technique IDs parsed from Sigma 'attack.tXXXX' tags or YARA meta.

false_positives.description: The rule's own documented FP conditions - shown to the analyst so a benign hit can be dismissed quickly.

match_detail.description: Engine-specific evidence: YARA string name, Sigma matched field, Nuclei matcher name.

match_offset.description: Byte offset of a YARA string match.

severity_max.description: Highest severity among detections[], or 'none'. Denormalized so CSV consumers and dashboards can sort without parsing the array.

provenance.description: Where this row came from inside the acquisition ZIP, so every timeline row is traceable to raw evidence.

raw_file.description: Path within the output ZIP, e.g. raw/Windows.NTFS.MFT/results.json.

extra.description: Source-specific fields that have no first-class home. Keys are sorted when serialized so output stays byte-stable.

x-csv-projection.description: timeline.csv column order. Nested objects are flattened with '_' and arrays joined with '; '. UTF-8 with BOM and CRLF so Excel and Eric Zimmerman's Timeline Explorer open it correctly without an import wizard.

derivedColumns.detection_severities: detections[].severity joined with '; ', index-aligned with detection_rules
derivedColumns.mitre_techniques: unique, sorted union of detections[].mitre_techniques joined with '; '
